subject: Inference deep-dive synthesis & commitments
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Elaine Park <elaine@carbide.ai>, Samir Qureshi <samir@carbide.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Apr 2027 15:08:00 -0700
Subject: Inference deep-dive synthesis & commitments

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick write-up to capture the facts we agreed on, the core pain, and the commitments we discussed so the team can move to a sizing/POC plan. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points (what we heard):
- p95 latency spikes during 9am-11am ET business surge; impacts interactive search and content generation flows.
- High token cost on the current managed endpoint — desire to reduce per-call spend without sacrificing quality.
- Failure modes: KV cache misses during traffic bursts and queueing on cold KV loads.

Business goals / acceptance criteria you stated:
- Maintain interactive UX: p95 <= 300ms for 64-token responses (short responses), and p95 <= 750ms for longer 512-token batched jobs.
- Support sustained peak of ~250 QPS with average payload ~48 tokens/request.
- Reduce per-token inference cost by ~35% vs current managed endpoint within 90 days of deployment.
- Successful end-to-end integration: rollout on Prod for 2 user-facing features with annotated quality tests and no regressions.

Model & workload notes from call:
- Primary model family: open-weights 30B–70B family for generation. You indicated preference for a 30B quantized variant for latency-critical routes and a 70B for highest-quality offline/long-form tasks.
- Average response length observed in telemetry: 44 tokens; tail up to ~800 tokens for batch summarization jobs.

Deployment topology we recommended and that we agreed to evaluate:
1) Tiered topology: Hosted Redwood API for day-0 integration + Dedicated pool for peak traffic (autoscaled reserved nodes) with policy-based routing (latency-first).
2) KV prefix caching at the edge for prompt prefixes (50–60% hit expected on structured prompts) to cut compute.
3) Quantized 30B variant on Dedicated A100-80GB pool for latency routes; 70B mixed-precision on burst nodes for batch/quality paths.
4) Fallback policy to lower-cost quantized 30B model in the unlikely case of Dedicated capacity exhaustion.

SLOs & sizing assumptions (engineering baseline):
- Target SLOs: p50 90–120ms, p95 <= 300ms for 64-token gen on dedicated 30B quantized; for 512-token gen p95 <= 700ms.
- Throughput: peak 250 QPS -> baseline dedicated pool of 6 x A100-80GB (estimate) with continuous batching and 2:1 safety buffer.
- KV cache hit assumed 55% after warm-up; reduces token compute ~40% at peak.

Immediate next steps / owners (agreed):
- Redwood to produce a constrained capacity/latency sizing sketch and cost delta (Jordan) — deliver by 2027-04-20 EOD.
- Carbide to share two weeks of anonymized telemetry (QPS, p50/p95, token distribution) and a sample prompt set for regression tests (Elaine / Samir) — target 2027-04-22.
- Redwood infra to validate KV cache policy options and include expected warm-up plan (Dev) — 2027-04-23.
- Schedule a 60-minute technical POC kickoff to align infra, security, and procurement (Grace) — propose slot week of 2027-04-26.

Attachments in this thread: redwood-slo-options.pdf (options matrix), carb ide-capacity-model.xlsx (initial sizing model), architecture-diagram-v1.png

If that all looks right I'll turn this into a one-pager and a HubSpot task list. Thanks again — next communication will be the sizing sketch (Jordan).

Best,

Jordan — thanks for the clear write-up, this matches our notes. A couple of clarifications:
- The p95 figures are for user-facing interactive API calls only; our background summarization batch jobs are allowed higher latency (we suggested up to 1.5s p95 at peak).
- For the model family, think of 30B quantized as our first target to validate cost/latency tradeoffs; we will only move to 70B after we confirm quality via the regression set.

Action on our side: procurement@carbide.ai will start the vendor intake once we have the expected committed spend range from your sizing sketch. I'll upload the telemetry by 2027-04-21 COB. Samir will send a redacted sample prompt set this afternoon.

—Elaine

Quick feasibility note from infra: initial sizing looks achievable with 6–8 A100-80GB equivalents for the 30B quantized path given continuous batching and 55% KV hit. Two quick asks that will materially change sizing:
1) Please include 14 days of QPS by hour (we want the diurnal curve) rather than just peak QPS — that can reduce buffer requirements.
2) We need a sample of your longest 25 prompts (the tail) so we can validate KV behavior for long prefixes.

I'll follow up after I run the sizing model with the two items.
